name: Akron
takeaway: Dynegy's Akron community page posts 9.95¢/kWh, 100% carbon-free, June 2026 through June 2028. The city's March 2025 release, still on the utilities page, describes the prior contract at 9.24¢ from May 2025 through June 2026. A third source for 9.95¢ was not found, so the stored zone rate is still 9.24¢.
hook: Akron's Dynegy page shows 9.95¢ through June 2028. The city page still describes 9.24¢ through June 2026. Read the bill before quoting either number.
notes: Current supplier: Dynegy at 9.24¢/kWh. Term ends approximately June 2026. Ohio Edison territory. Verify exact term end date and new program rate. Note: Cuyahoga Falls and Wadsworth are municipal electric utilities — not eligible for competitive electric supply.

name: Green
takeaway: Green's city electric page posts a NOPEC fixed price of 9.48¢/kWh for 12 months starting June 2026, for residents and businesses, on Ohio Edison. The zone file still lists Dynegy at 9.24¢ through June 30, 2026.
hook: Green's city page is NOPEC at 9.48¢ fixed from June 2026, including businesses. The zone file still shows the prior Dynegy price of 9.24¢.
notes: Green City, Summit County. Same Dynegy/Ohio Edison program as Akron. Term end approximately June 2026. Strong commercial/retail growth on SR-241.

name: Medina County
takeaway: Medina County's Dynegy aggregation is stored at 9.5¢/kWh from May 1, 2026 through June 30, 2028, prior price 6.05¢. Cities with their own programs, including Medina and Brunswick, are separate.
hook: Medina County Dynegy is 9.5¢ through June 2028 on this record. Confirm the account is in the county program and not a city deal.
notes: Medina County aggregation program (separate from NOPEC). Rate: 9.50¢/kWh, confirmed active May 2026 through June 2028. Ohio Edison territory. Accounts that opted out of the county program may be on a higher standard offer rate. Cities and villages are ineligible. This is the unincorporated county program.

name: Stark County (Unincorporated / Remaining)
takeaway: No county-wide program. Unincorporated Stark County is split by township.
notes: Jackson Township (Stark) and Perry Township (Stark) are Dynegy programs. Plain Township and Paris Township (Stark) are NOPEC members.

name: Kent / Portage County
takeaway: Kent is on the NOPEC standard program at 10.399¢/kWh, variable, from the September 2026 meter read through the June 2027 meter read. This is not a countywide Portage price. No early termination fee. The prior standard price was 9.999¢ for the June through August 2026 meter reads. Eligible residential and small-business accounts are enrolled unless they opted out or chose a fixed term (12-month 10.299¢, 24-month 10.599¢). Larger mercantile accounts are outside the aggregation.
hook: Kent small accounts on the NOPEC default are at 10.399¢ through the June 2027 meter read, no exit fee, up from 9.999¢. This is the city, not all of Portage County. Ask whether the larger meters opted out.
notes: NOPEC standard 10.399¢/kWh variable, September 2026 through June 2027 meter reads, no exit fee. Prior standard price 9.999¢ for June through August 2026 meter reads. Kent and surrounding Portage County communities are NOPEC members. Ohio Edison territory. University/commercial mix in Kent proper.

name: Clinton
takeaway: NOPEC's community map lists Clinton Village as an electric member, and the research card carries the 10.399¢ standard price. The zone file still says no aggregation and has no rate. A village notice was not in the sources checked on October 21, 2026, so the file was left as it is.
hook: Clinton is on NOPEC's member map. This file has no rate. Read the bill before quoting the standard price.
notes: Village of Clinton, Summit County (not Clinton County). Located near 2534 W Comet Rd area. Ohio Edison service area. No municipal or township aggregation program found. Sits in Akron/Canton commercial orbit. Use Medina County pain story or Akron renewal story when prospecting in this corridor.
